title: Ontario Opens Applications for New Workforce Priority Stream, Replacing All Previous Immigration Pathways
excerpt: Canada's most populous province launches its first new permanent residence pathway since sunsetting all prior OINP streams in May, with three tracks for skilled workers, lower-skilled workers, and physicians.
body:
• Ontario opened its new Workforce Priority Stream on August 4, 2026, the first replacement pathway after sunsetting all previous OINP immigration streams on May 30.
  • The stream has three tracks: higher-skilled workers, lower-skilled workers, and self-employed physicians registered to practice in Ontario.
  • Applicants need a qualifying job offer from an Ontario employer and must create an Expression of Interest in the province's e-Filing Portal; candidates are ranked under a points-based scoring system.
  • Three additional streams — healthcare workers, entrepreneurs, and exceptional talent — are planned for a second phase, though launch dates have not been announced.

Ontario has finally opened the door to its overhauled provincial immigration system, launching the Workforce Priority Stream on Tuesday after months of uncertainty that left thousands of foreign nationals in limbo.

What's New

The Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program posted the opening on its program updates page, activating the e-Filing Portal where eligible foreign nationals can now submit Expressions of Interest. It marks the first functioning pathway since the province controversially sunset all its previous immigration streams on May 30, 2026, without any replacements in place.

https://x.com/canadavisa_com/status/2084729566770209169

The OWPS operates through three distinct tracks. The higher-skilled worker pathway targets professionals in occupations that Ontario has identified as in demand. The lower-skilled worker pathway opens a route for workers in sectors like manufacturing, agriculture, and construction that have historically struggled to attract permanent residents. A third track covers self-employed physicians registered to bill Ontario's public health insurance program, OHIP.

How It Works

The process begins with an Ontario employer creating a qualifying job offer in the OINP's Employer Portal. The foreign national then files an Expression of Interest linked to that job offer. Ontario periodically draws from the pool of active EOIs using a points-based scoring system that the province published on July 20.

EOIs remain valid for 12 months. If a candidate doesn't receive an invitation to apply within that window, they must re-register. Successful candidates in the higher-skilled stream can apply through Express Entry, potentially accessing faster federal processing.

"The OWPS is the first to launch of Ontario's new provincial immigration pathways, as part of the first phase of the province's planned overhaul of the OINP."

— Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program update

What Comes Next

Ontario has announced three additional streams under a planned second phase: a priority healthcare worker stream, an entrepreneur stream, and an exceptional talent stream focused on foreign nationals with significant achievements in academia, innovation, science, technology, or the arts. The province has not published full eligibility details or launch dates for any of these.

Why It Matters for Indian Applicants

Ontario receives more Indian immigrants than any other Canadian province. The two-month gap between the old streams closing and the new one opening created real anxiety among Indian nationals already working in Ontario on temporary permits, particularly those whose work permit renewals or LMIA applications were caught in transition.

The points-based scoring system adds a new variable. Unlike the previous streams, which operated largely on a first-come, first-served basis, the OWPS will rank candidates competitively. For Indian applicants, strong language scores, Canadian work experience, and employer-backed job offers will be critical differentiators.

Applicants who had already submitted applications under the now-defunct streams will have those assessed under the old criteria — a small comfort for those who got in before the May cutoff. Everyone else enters a new system that Ontario is still building in real time.
